title: Stop the dispatcher from using up the courier service's rate limit

blocks.text: The dispatcher decides which courier gets each delivery job, and the shop page asks it whether a zone can be promised delivery within the hour. Both questions go to the courier service, which allows a fixed number of requests per minute. Since the dispatcher was rewritten, the service has started refusing requests at lunchtime, when the zone lists are longest.
`Dispatcher` already assigns jobs and answers the shop page. Finish the two `TODO`s in `src/main/java/practice/Dispatcher.java`:

items: `nearestFree(...)`: the first free courier of a list sorted nearest first;
`anyFree(...)`: whether anyone in a list is free.

blocks.text: When you're done, both give the same answers as before, and neither asks the service about a courier whose answer can no longer change the result. About two lines in total.

cases.says: a job goes to the nearest courier the service reports as free
when no courier is free the job is queued
fast delivery is promised exactly when at least one courier in the zone is free
assigning a job asks the service about couriers only up to the one who gets the job
the fast-delivery check stops asking the service at the first free courier

origin.section: Each Element Goes Through the Whole Pipeline Before the Next, and Short-Circuiting Stops the Pulling

concepts: A short-circuiting operation such as findFirst or anyMatch stops pulling elements once it has its answer, while collecting first or counting reads every element.
